body_markdown:
Few events get us more excited about seeing off-road adventure rigs and lowered street trucks than the annual SEMA show. Even if we know that the extreme crawlers and desert runners are way beyond our means, or even what is practical, we’re always inspired by the innovation that their talented creators show off each year. Here are some unique builds that stood out at SEMA 2026 that we were able to dig into, plus a gallery of other trucks that piqued our interest.


## Weaver Customs 1959 Suburban


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


Randy and Sydney Weaver, owners of Weaver Customs just outside of Salt Lake City, usually have a handful of builds going on at any given time. While their customers’ builds are moving along, they often have a project on the back burner that Randy or Sydney enjoys for a year or so before they sell it and move on. That’s the plan for this 1959 Suburban 4×4. Randy built it as a fun outdoor toy. Like an overgrown shooting brake, there’s room in the back in the custom drawer for a pair of over/unders for sporting clays. The LS1 under the hood provides plenty of power using a Holley EFI system and an Edelbrock Pro-Flo intake manifold. Randy told us that despite Chevy trucks having a deep aftermarket for restoration parts, there were plenty of pieces on a Suburban that had to be custom-made, like the quarter panels. Luckily, Randy discovered that the cable mechanisms for lowering the tailgate could be easily swapped for those from a Nomad, which are reproduced. Still, lots of this big wagon had to be hand-fabricated. The results are worth it, however, and the understated 4×4 should have no trouble finding a new home when it heads to auction in 2027.

## Jeep Scrambler Concept


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


The Scrambler is a throwback to the long-wheelbase CJ8 from the ‘80s, and this one packs some surprises. Most notably, it features a second row of seats that can face forward or backward. It’s also got a one-off independent front suspension to further separate it from the rest of the Jeep crowd. With 37-inch tires and some beefy suspension components, the custom independent front suspension seems capable of handling low-speed crawling over tough trails as well as soaking up high-speed dirt roads and desert runs. Its 392 Hemi V-8 would provide enough power and torque to handle either task. Jeep continues to show off Wrangler-based builds with amazing, M715-inspired front ends; it seems cruel to tease it so much and not offer one on the showroom floor.

## 1976 Jeep Honcho


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


Tony Carvallo from Brass Barn Customs has built 16 SEMA feature vehicles so far. His latest is this 1976 Jeep J10 Honcho, which was customized for his friend Josh, owner of Off the Grid Surplus. It’s still powered by an AMC 360 V-8, but it uses a Holley Sniper EFI conversion. It rides on a late-model Jeep Wrangler chassis that’s been stretched five inches. The Jeep chassis allowed for a wide selection of aftermarket parts, including Steer Smarts steering linkage, PSC hydraulic assist, Ultimate Dana 60 axles front and rear, and new, longer control arms. It rides on 40-inch Milestar Patagonia tires mounted to Raceline wheels and has Fox three-inch internal-bypass shocks at each corner.

The process of cutting and folding new wheel openings allowed the Jeep to keep its sun-baked original paint. Carvallo bent the metal back a little at a time using an adjustable wrench to clamp down on the sheet metal and provide leverage. “It took me, no joke, two to three hours for each corner,” said Carvallo. The paint on the vintage camper shell was aged to better match the truck, as Cavallo applied several layers of paint and red oxide primer so that it could be scuffed a bit to match the truck.


## 1965 Chevy C10/K30


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


Bryan Howell’s 1965 Chevy started life as a C10 and has been in his family since it was purchased new by his great-uncle, who then sold it to his grandfather. Next, his father owned it, and it was a project truck for years. Its current iteration was Bryan’s doing, and he admitted that he “maybe went a little bit over the top.” That’s fine by us.


Now that it’s a 4×4, the ’65 Chevy uses a Dynatrac ProRock 80 rear axle and a ProRock 60 front axle. It rides on 40-inch tires. “Dave Chappelle from Dirthead Shed went through and boxed the entire frame,” explained Bryan. The truck still has trailing arms in the rear, but nothing like the original Chevy parts. Now it resembles a Trophy Truck. It’s powered by an LSA V-8 from a Cadillac CTS-V, along with its 6L80 E transmission. The paint is the same color as the truck’s original, which Chevy called “Fawn”.

## Ford Bronco Frostwarden


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


Powered by Ford’s newest supercharged 7.3-liter Godzilla V-8 crate engine, this search-and-rescue Bronco now has 1200 horsepower. Dubbed Megazilla 2.0, the crate engine supplies more than 1000 lb-ft. of torque and offers a broad powerband thanks to its 3.0L Whipple supercharger. That’s beyond impressive, but the Bronco isn’t just about ponies. With 42-inch tires and 74Weld portals at each corner, it brings tremendous ground clearance and the grip to scramble over anything it can’t straddle. We’re not sure that 1200 hp is necessary in an off-road rescue vehicle, but SEMA builds are competing in an attention economy. There’s so much here to grab eyes that it can’t hurt to go big.

## 1994 Toyota 4×4


[Brandan Gillogly](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/brandan-gillogly/)


On the other side of the coin, this well-preserved Toyota at the Yakima booth shows that you don’t need a lot of custom fabrication to set off a build if it looks like it drove out of a time capsule. Aside from some understated new wheels and fresh BF Goodrich rubber, everything aside from its bed-mounted Yakima accessories was stock. The 100,000-mile truck was treated to a Yakima OverHaul HD rack fitted with a Supdawg mount for a surfboard, a Roadshower 4G for rinsing off the salt, and storage for plenty of fishing rods. A StepUp swingout bike rack also helps out by handling a pair of bicycles or e-bikes.
